answer_text:
Let

\[
\alpha=\overline{x}\in K=\mathbb{F}_2[x]/(x^3+x+1).
\]

Then \(\alpha\) satisfies

\[
\alpha^3+\alpha+1=0.
\]

We want the minimal polynomial of

\[
\overline{x+1}=\alpha+1
\]

over \(\mathbb{F}_2\). Let

\[
\beta=\alpha+1.
\]

Then

\[
\alpha=\beta+1.
\]

Substitute this into \(\alpha^3+\alpha+1=0\):

\[
(\beta+1)^3+(\beta+1)+1=0.
\]

Since we are working over \(\mathbb{F}_2\), we have \((\beta+1)^3=\beta^3+\beta^2+\beta+1\). Therefore,

\[
\beta^3+\beta^2+\beta+1+\beta+1+1=0.
\]

Simplifying in characteristic \(2\),

\[
\beta^3+\beta^2+1=0.
\]

Thus \(\beta=\overline{x+1}\) is a root of

\[
f(t)=t^3+t^2+1.
\]

This polynomial is irreducible over \(\mathbb{F}_2\) because it has no roots in \(\mathbb{F}_2\):

\[
f(0)=1,\qquad f(1)=1+1+1=1.
\]

Since \(\overline{x+1}\notin \mathbb{F}_2\), its minimal polynomial must have degree \(3\), so it is exactly \(f(t)\).

\[
\boxed{t^3+t^2+1}
\]
